name: Wednesday Night WarZone

matches.stipulation: World Heavyweight Championship Tournament, First Round
matches.note: Hardcastle won by pinfall with a top-rope splash, after Vars's valet Cindy was accidentally kissed unconscious mid-match and later tripped Vars during a comeback attempt.

matches.stipulation: World Heavyweight Championship Tournament, First Round
matches.note: The main event. Walsh won by submission (the Gas Chamber) after a superplex through an outside table and a chair shot on Wallace from Walsh's own manager, Bishop.

notes: The broadcast opens with two roster notices not carried into matches[]: a wrestler named Steve Rodman was reported fired for a drug violation (giving Aaron Farner, unminted, a National Title tournament bye), and a tag team called Shwag was reported to be taking time off (giving a team called The Enforcers, unminted, a bye to the tag title tournament final). Neither bye match nor either unminted team is structured.

name: Saturday Night Showcase

date.source: The show's own text dates itself "4\/25\/98"; posted in seven parts to rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy on 26 April 1998.

appearances.note: Opens the broadcast reinstating Steve Rodman and announcing the vacant Tag Team Title match and a coming National Title battle royal.
His own stable, The Professionals, distracts the referee and helps Jinsei Shakanuzi retain.

matches.note: Shakanuzi won by pinfall (a top-rope tigerdriver) after his own stable, The Professionals, distracted the referee and struck Collins with a chair.

matches.stipulation: World Heavyweight Championship Tournament, First Round

matches.stipulation: World Heavyweight Championship Tournament, First Round

notes: The broadcast's own opening promo also gives Aaron Farner a bye into the National Title Tournament's second round (Steve Rodman's own drug-testing suspension having been lifted rather than upheld, per an earlier broadcast) and The Enforcers a bye to the Tag Team Title final before their own release from the roster is announced moments later; neither bye match nor the unminted Enforcers are structured.

matches.stipulation: Juniorweight Championship Number-One-Contender Match, Best of Three Falls
matches.note: Wildcat stole the first fall with a victory roll, but Wardancer came back to win the match and the number-one contendership.
Wallace won by pinfall in 30 minutes with his own finisher, "the Heartbreaker," despite fighting both men alone for most of the match.
Mad Goat won the title from the champion Jinsei Shakanuzi.
Williams won the pin after National Champion Setzer Van Strife ran in with a chair and knocked out the referee's count for him, costing Floyd a match he had otherwise won clean.

Robinson won the match by disqualification after Nat Richards ran in and attacked him mid-pin, but the champion Van Strife retained the title, since a title cannot change hands on a disqualification finish.
Walsh won by pinfall with a top-rope DDT after nearly an hour, becoming the promotion's first-ever World Heavyweight Champion.

notes: The broadcast's own four-way dance deciding Teen Angst's own title shot (against three further, unminted teams) and its own undercard Free-For-All tag match are described but not structured, for want of a complete, confirmed roster on every side.

name: Boston Massacre

date.source: The show's own eight posted parts, all dated 27 June 1998 to rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy, from the promotion's own Fleet Center broadcast.

appearances.note: Interferes in the Wallace/Meanor match with his own National Title belt, without preventing Wallace's win.
Pinned alongside a beaten Candyman by Glamour and Extreme for the deciding fall.

matches.note: Teen Angst won the titles after Cobain rang the timekeeper's bell on his own partner Vedder to fake a distraction, then pinned a battered Max Studd.
Mad Goat retained the title.
Wallace won by pinfall (a piledriver, "the Heart Attack") in 17 minutes 32 seconds, despite National Champion Setzer Van Strife running in to hit him with the title belt mid-match.

Glamour and Extreme won by pinfall after Al Robertson turned on his own partner Candyman with a garbage can, and Matt Blazer (unminted) used a pair of brass knuckles on Candyman before Glamour pinned both Candyman and his valet Candyfloss at once.

Creed, revealed as Team Williams's own mystery fourth man, ended it by spraying Brian Floyd with a chemical from an aerosol can, knocking him out with a wooden chair, and locking on a camel clutch for the submission; Iron Spike used brass knuckles and Williams used a baseball bat, both smuggled in by Creed, earlier in the fall.

notes: The broadcast's own commentary flags continuity slips left on the record as broadcast: it introduces the challenger, Ivan Ramieus, as facing Mad Goat for the same title "he actually won it from" Jinsei Shakanuzi, and a backstage vignette reveals Christian Hardcastle's alter ego "Da Yellow Guy" without further explanation.

name: Saturday Night Showcase

date.source: No date appears in the broadcast's own text; its own recap of the previous night's War Games places it the night after Boston Massacre (27 June 1998), and its own ten parts were first posted to rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy on 29 June 1998, with several parts retried through 13 July 1998 after apparent posting failures.

appearances.note: Distracts Lawrence Williams in the Chicago Street Fight main event, letting Brock Carden win with a chair-assisted power bomb.
Runs in unexplained and chokeslams Aries during the Creed match, costing him the finish.
Defeats the unminted Robert Hearsch by pinfall.
Defeats the unminted Aaron "Wildfire" Farner.
Defeats the unminted Dark Vanity by pinfall.
Loses to "Brutal" Brian Floyd.
Defeats Jack Vars by pinfall.
Loses to the unminted Nikodemous Segier.
Teen Angst retain the World Tag Team Championship against the unminted challengers Rod Renson and Andrew "Flash" Tucker.
Teen Angst retain the World Tag Team Championship against the unminted challengers Rod Renson and Andrew "Flash" Tucker.
Teams with forced partner Mister Meanor to win a Love/Hate Tag Team Match over Ian Walsh and the unminted Ryan Justice.
Teams with forced partner Steve Wallace to win a Love/Hate Tag Team Match over Ian Walsh and the unminted Ryan Justice.
Runs in after the Street Fight and attacks the beaten Brian Floyd with a chair.

Announces the full Summer Bash 98 card (Walsh defends against Williams; a Three Way Dance; Van Strife defends the National Title against Wallace in a Ladder Match) and a separate number-one-contender tournament toward "Fall Breakout 98" in September.

matches.note: Carden won by pinfall with a chair-assisted power bomb after champion Ian Walsh, at ringside, distracted Williams at a key moment; both men had earlier no-sold multiple near-falls, including Williams kicking out of a superplex through a table.
Cary won the match by countout in 14 minutes 42 seconds, but champion Van Strife retained the title, since a title cannot change hands on a countout finish.
Creed pinned an exhausted Aries after Doomsday ran in unexplained and chokeslammed Aries out of his own finishing sequence.

notes: The promotion's own final surviving broadcast opens with a replay of the previous night's War Games finish (Creed revealed as the mystery fourth man, arming his own team with smuggled brass knuckles, a chair and a baseball bat before Brian Floyd's submission) -- evidence for Boston Massacre's own record, not restructured here. President Jay's own closing promo announces a number-one-contender tournament toward a September supercard, "Fall Breakout 98," whose own remaining rounds this collection's own corpus does not reach; "Summer Bash 98" itself (26 July 1998), the card this broadcast spends its own runtime building toward, is likewise never reached -- the collection's own further posts run only to recruitment and administrative material through 31 July 1998, one of which states plainly that the promotion's own president "is out of E-wrestling completely." Five further undercard matches (Robert Hearsch/Johnny Glamour, Aaron Farner/Candyman, Dark Vanity/Whog Shrog, Jack Vars/Brian Floyd, "Wildcat" Jim Lewis Jr./Nikodemous Segier) and the Tag Team Title defense and Love\/Hate tag match are described in the appearances above but not structured into matches[], for want of a confirmed opponent on the other side.
